test_focus: metaphor-wrapper ablation — same 7 technical-debugging scenarios as Phase 10, but a 3-arm experiment: control vs current 'dreams' wrapper vs new 'neutral' wrapper.
tester: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context), live as the developer

implementation_added.behavior_dreams: header='## You appear to be stuck. Here is some imagination.', preface mentions 'dreams', items labelled 'Fragment N', 'Tonight I dreamed of' titles preserved
implementation_added.behavior_neutral: header='## Additional context', preface neutral, items labelled 'Observation N', 'Tonight I dreamed of' prefixes stripped via _strip_dream_prefix

experiment_design.scenario_types: same 7 technical-debugging scenarios as Phase 10 (chmod permission-denied, Python memory creep, flaky-CI test, slow prod query, refactor decision, retry-under-load, legacy-code deletion)
experiment_design.judge_comparisons: Two head-to-head judgments per scenario: Control vs Dreams, and Control vs Neutral. Did not directly judge Dreams vs Neutral.
experiment_design.blinding: response order randomized per comparison via the seeded RNG

results.verdict_summary: Both treatment arms beat control more often than not on the same scenario set Phase 10 had control winning 6/7. The neutral wrapper is not decisively better than dreams. The most-important finding is the variance: Phase 10 said treatment-with-dreams wins 1/7, Phase 12 same scenarios said treatment-with-dreams wins 5/7.

implications: **Phase 10 vs Phase 12 reveals substantial run-to-run variance.** Same scenarios, same wrapper, opposite outcomes: P10 had control winning 6/7 against dreams, P12 has dreams winning 5/7. The TRUE effect size on technical-debugging prompts is much smaller than P10 headlines suggested.
The neutral wrapper is not decisively better than the dreams wrapper on technical prompts (4 vs 5 wins). Stripping the metaphor doesn't fix anything important.
Phase 11's 6/7 creative-prompt result is sturdier — the larger margin survives across runs, and the consistency of the judge's reasoning (rewarding evocative reframes) is the real signal.

Lesson: at N=7 with stochastic LLMs and a stochastic judge, ±2 wins of noise is normal. Phase 10's headline was correct DIRECTIONALLY (treatment is weaker on technical) but its magnitude was overstated.

Recommendation: in the context-aware design that ships in this commit, use the neutral wrapper for engineering/research/general agents not because it's clearly better but because it's at least not WORSE and it removes a known irritant ('Fragment from your dreams' framing). Use the dreams wrapper for creative agents because Phase 11 evidence is strong.

feature_verdicts.imagination_injection_dreams_style: noisy on technical prompts — Phase 10 said -, Phase 12 said +
feature_verdicts.imagination_injection_neutral_style: roughly equivalent to dreams on technical prompts; preserves the option to ship

known_limitations: N=7 is too small to distinguish a marginal effect from noise (this phase's main lesson)
verdict: MIXED — neutral wrapper does not materially improve outcomes, but it's the safer default for non-creative agents and ships clean.
next_steps: Phase 13 (suggested): mixed-scenario set, single agent profile pinned engineering. Verify the new classifier routes correctly.
Phase 14 (suggested): N=30 per scenario class for proper statistical power.
